blocks.x: Welcome to What’s On, our weekly roundup of notable shows. Here is what’s happening on TV from Sunday, October 4 to Saturday, October 10. All times are Eastern.

Small Prophets (Apple TV, Wednesday, series premiere) After premiering in the U.K. in February, this weird little wonder has made its way across the pond and brought all of its quirky magical realism with it. Created, written, and directed by Mackenzie Crook, the story follows Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley), a hardware store worker living in a Manchester cul-de-sac and grieving the disappearance of his partner Clea seven years prior. With the support of his eccentric dad Brian (Michael Palin), Sleep sets out to create homunculi—tiny, prophesying beings that reside in glass jars full of water (rendered here via stop-motion animation)—to find out what happened to Clea. Read The A.V. Club’s take on the series on Tuesday.

Below (Netflix, Thursday, series premiere) Josh Hartnett captains this six-episode Canadian thriller, whose logline is giving Widow’s Bay with the Jaws levels turned way up: Hartnett plays Calvin Penney, a hard-bitten fisherman living in a remote Newfoundland community that’s being terrorized by a mysterious, violent sea creature lurking in the local waters. Determined to keep his son Wade (Charlie Heaton) safe and protect their community, Calvin teams up with a visiting marine biologist (Mackenzie Davis) to uncover the dark secrets hidden deep in the ocean. Find The A.V. Club’s series review on Thursday.

Eternally Yours (CBS, Thursday, 8:30 p.m., series premiere) Marriages are bound to fall into a bit of a rut after some years—but imagine being wed to someone for centuries. Such is the case for Charles (Ed Weeks) and Liz (Allegra Edwards), a married vampire couple who have been together for 500 years, only to find their once-passionate hot-and-heavy romance has turned bloodless and stale. That monotonous routine gets a welcome jolt when their daughter Emma (Helen J. Shen) brings home her very earnest and very human boyfriend Max (Jaren Lewison). The single-cam, half-hour sitcom comes from Ghosts’ Joe Port and Joe Wiseman, and also stars Parker Young, Rose Abdoo, and Jeff Hiller. Check out The A.V. Club’s review on Monday.

Avatar: Seven Havens (Paramount+, Friday, series premiere) A sequel to Avatar: The Last Airbender and The Legend Of Korra, this action-fantasy animated series centers on Pavi (voiced by Saheli Khan), a nine-year-old Earthbender living in the city of Ellora, who learns that she is the next Avatar after Korra. Facing a world shattered by a devastating cataclysm and marked as a destroyer instead of a savior, she sets out with her long-lost twin sister Nisha (Aishu Devan) to uncover their mysterious origins and save the Seven Havens upon which the future of humanity hinges. The first three episodes premiere on Friday; you can also find The A.V. Club’s review that day.

Ted Lasso (Apple TV, Wednesday, season four finale)
Last Seen (Apple TV, Wednesday, season one finale)
JAŸ-Z IN 8 (HBO, Friday, 8 p.m., docuseries finale)
Anna Pigeon (USA Network, Friday, 10 p.m., season one finale)
